# altalt

A friendly setup guide for connecting [Alt](https://altalt.io) notes to an AI
app or a custom integration.

```bash
npx altalt
```

The guide uses Korean when your system language is Korean and English
otherwise. You can override it with `--lang ko` or `--lang en`.

## Easy AI app connection

If you do not plan to use an API or webhook directly, the guide detects
Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor and lets you choose one app at a time. Technical
terms such as MCP and OAuth stay out of the main flow; browser sign-in and the
next action are explained when needed.

For another AI app, choose **Other AI app**. The guide shows the public remote
HTTP MCP address, offers to copy it, and explains where to paste it. The app
must support remote HTTP MCP and browser authentication.

Existing Alt connections are kept by default. You can explicitly add a new
browser-login connection beside an existing one, but the guide never removes
or overwrites an MCP connection.

After setup, try asking your AI app:

> Show my recent Alt notes.

## Developer setup

Choose the developer path when you want to use the REST API or webhooks
directly. API, webhook, and combined setup are separate so each path requests
and verifies only the required permissions:

- API: `notes:read`, `transcripts:read`, `summaries:read`
- Webhooks: `webhooks:manage`
- Both: all four permissions

The guide verifies the key before changing files. Inside a recognized project,
it shows the exact `.env` path and asks for confirmation before writing. Outside
a project, it never writes the key to disk. It also refuses to put a key in an
`.env` file that Git already tracks. Webhook test events are opt-in and require
a final confirmation.

The optional coding-agent handoff appears only in the developer path. Declining
it does not print a long implementation prompt.

## Options

```text
--mcp-only       go directly to AI app connection
--api-only       go directly to API/webhook setup
--lang ko|en     choose the display language
--verbose        show technical command and API errors
--print-prompt   print the coding-agent prompt and exit
--dev            target the development stack for pre-release QA
--version        print the package version
--help           show help
```

Interactive terminals use an arrow-key menu. Piped input remains supported with
numbered choices for scripts and automated checks.

Docs: https://altalt.io/developers
